title: Solar Photovoltaic
description: Becquerel's 1839 effect to Bell Labs' 1954 cell: the semiconductor technology that became the cheapest new power in history.

title: Onshore Wind
description: Modern three-blade turbines: 35%+ capacity factors and the backbone of renewable grids from Texas to the North Sea coast.

title: Hydropower
description: The oldest and still largest renewable: falling water through turbines, from Niagara (1895) to the Three Gorges.

title: Geothermal
description: Earth's heat as baseload power: Larderello 1904 to Iceland's grids and Kenya's Rift Valley expansion.

title: Tidal Stream
description: Underwater windmills in tidal races: La Rance (1966), MeyGen, and the predictable power of the tides.

title: Biomass Energy
description: The oldest fuel made modern: solid biomass, biogas, and the carbon-accounting debate around it.

title: Green Hydrogen
description: Hydrogen from water electrolysis powered by renewables: the storable fuel for steel, ships, and seasonal grids.

title: Concentrated Solar Power
description: Mirrors and heat, not panels: Ivanpah, Noor, and molten-salt storage that lets the sun shine at night.
